title: Stochastic binary networks with asymmetric and time-delayed interactions
authors: Hantao Zhang, Sidra Gibeault, Matthew W. Daniels, Philippe Talatchian, Ursula Ebels, Advait Madhavan, Mark D. Stiles
abstract: Stochastic binary networks are widely used to describe collective dynamics in complex systems and to perform neuromorphic computation, yet realistic networks often contain both asymmetric interactions and finite signal propagation times that fall outside conventional theories. Here we study stochastic binary networks with asymmetric and time-delayed interactions motivated by experimental observations in coupled superparamagnetic tunnel junctions. We find that time delay fundamentally reshapes the dynamics induced by anti-symmetric couplings, producing strong oscillatory temporal correlations consistent with experiment. At the same time, sufficiently long delays drive the steady-state probabilities toward equal state occupations even in strongly coupled systems. These apparently featureless probability distributions coexist with pronounced temporal correlations, distinguishing them from equilibrium high-temperature behavior. We further show analytically that delay-induced uniform distributions emerge in a broad class of stochastic networks, while symmetry-breaking bias fields restore interaction-dependent steady states with qualitatively modified behavior. Simulations of networks with five coupled spins demonstrate that these effects persist beyond minimal systems with only two spins. Our results establish a unified framework for stochastic binary networks in the intermediate regime between symmetric instantaneous interactions and asymmetric or time-delayed interactions, and suggest that asymmetry and delay can be exploited as functional resources in neuromorphic hardware and complex network dynamics.
summary: This paper analyzes stochastic binary networks featuring asymmetric interactions and time delays, motivated by experiments on magnetic tunnel junctions. It demonstrates that these non-ideal features fundamentally alter system dynamics, leading to observable temporal oscillations or universal uniform steady states. The work establishes a general framework showing how asymmetry and delay can be harnessed as functional resources in complex network modeling.
main_problem: The study investigates stochastic binary networks incorporating both asymmetric interactions and finite time delays, features often neglected by conventional theoretical models.
main_result: Time delay fundamentally reshapes dynamics induced by anti-symmetric couplings, causing strong oscillations in temporal correlations. Furthermore, long delays drive the steady state toward uniform probability distributions unless symmetry is explicitly broken.
method: The authors combine theoretical analysis (deriving conditions for doubly stochastic matrices) with numerical simulations and comparisons to experimental data from coupled superparamagnetic tunnel junctions.
model_or_system:
The system is modeled using stochastic binary networks of Ising spins ($	ext{S}_i = \pm 1$) whose dynamics are governed by probabilistic updates incorporating time delays ($t_{i\leftarrow j}$) and non-reciprocal couplings ($J_{i\leftarrow j} 
eq J_{j\leftarrow i}$).
key_observables: Auto-correlation ($ho_{	ext{auto}}$) and cross-correlation ($ho_{	ext{cross}}$) functions, steady-state joint probability distributions, and the symmetry-breaking parameter $R_{\log}$.
important_parameters: Asymmetry in coupling ($J_{i\leftarrow j}$ vs $J_{j\leftarrow i}$) and the magnitude of time delays ($t_{i\leftarrow j}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending beyond simple Markov models, assuming global symmetry constraints for proving uniform steady states, and using approximations related to long delay times.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate experimental correlation data from SMTJs, compare simulation results for auto-correlation under different coupling regimes (FM, AFM, Asym), and show the dependence of the steady-state distribution on couplings and biases with long delays.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the limitations of standard models due to delay/asymmetry. It then presents theoretical results showing how these features induce oscillations or uniform distributions in the steady state, culminating in a unified framework applicable to neuromorphic hardware design.
why_interesting: The findings provide a detailed understanding of non-equilibrium dynamics in coupled systems where memory effects (delay) and directional coupling (asymmetry) are crucial, which is highly relevant for modeling complex physical or computational substrates.
